title: Cohort Throttle & Metrics Tally — Pre-launch prioritization lattice and contingency playbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, action-oriented sheet to guide a phased go-live using cohort-level throttles and a lean KPI tally. Designed for product-ops + SRE + oncall to execute decisions in the first 72 hours and scale confidently.

TL;DR (one paragraph):
- Launch in 4 cohorts (alpha, beta, early, open). Start traffic low and increase per the priority lattice below. Use the KPI tally to decide stair-step increases. Predefine firebreaks for latency, error-rate, and cost-per-1k tokens; if any firebreak trips, immediately rollback to the prior cohort allocation and run fast postmortem.

Cohort definitions (for this release):
- Cohort A — Internal alpha: 0.5% of production traffic, internal users + feature flags.
- Cohort B — Beta partners: 2.0% traffic, invited customers, higher SLO tolerance for noise.
- Cohort C — Early customers: 10% traffic, monitored + throttles for heavy tails.
- Cohort D — Open: remainder (gradual ramp to 100%).

Throttle tiers (allocation plan):
- Step 0 (smoke): A=0.5%, B=0%, C=0%, D=0% (sanity checks)
- Step 1: A=1.0%, B=0.5%, C=0%, D=0%
- Step 2: A=1.5%, B=1.5%, C=2.0%, D=0%
- Step 3: A=2.0%, B=3.0%, C=10.0%, D=5.0%
- Step 4: Gradual open with daily increments of +10–20% for D, pause if any firebreak trips

Priority lattice (how to pick next cohort to expand):
- Expand cohorts in order of highest quality signal where: (1) mean latency < target, (2) per-route error rate within threshold, (3) cost per 1k tokens within budget band.
- If two cohorts both meet signals, expand the smaller cohort first to reduce blast radius.

KPI tally (single-line format, update hourly in shared doc):
- Latency P95 (ms): target <= 420ms, warning 420–700ms, critical >700ms
- 5xx rate (all endpoints): target <= 0.3%, warning 0.3–1.0%, critical >1.0%
- Model-quality regression (eval set BLEU/ROUGE/semantic): no drop >3% absolute vs baseline
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD): target <= $0.85, warning $0.85–$1.25, critical >$1.25
- KV cache hit rate (inference): target >= 75% for repetitive workloads
- Error-observed-unique (new error classes last 24h): target 0, critical >=3 unique classes
- Customer-visible failures (support tickets referencing generation): target 0, warning >=1, critical >=5 within 1h

Example KPI row (timestamped manual snapshot):
- 2026-03-01 09:00 UTC | P95=390ms | 5xx=0.12% | model-regress=0.0% | $/1k=0.78 | cache=81% | unique-errors=0 | tickets=0 | stage=Step 2

Firebreak triggers (automated + human thresholds):
1) Automated immediate abort (system-enforced): 5xx>2.5% on global, or P99>1400ms sustained for 5m. Automation cuts new traffic to cohort D, falls back to Step 1 allocation.
2) Human-decision firebreak: any critical tag (model-quality regression >3%) or cost runaway >200% of expected for 30m — ops lead calls GO/NO-GO.
3) Hotline escalation: SRE oncall + product ops + eng-serving-runtime present for triage within 15m.

Owners & RACI (short):
- Product-Ops (Maya Chen): overall sequencing, comms, go/no-go decision owner
- SRE (Diego Morales): oncall, runbook execution, automation toggles
- Serving Runtime Eng (Asha Patel): model fallback, capacity knobs, kernel-level fixes
- Support (Liam O'Connor): ticket triage, customer comms

Runbook snippets (playbook steps for a single firebreak):
1) Alert fires: SRE oncall posts incident in #prod-ops and tags product-ops pager
2) Confirm signal (5m window): validate telemetry, sample traces, check recent deploys or infra changes
3) Action: reduce affected cohort(s) allocation by 50% and re-route to fallback model if available
4) Post-action validate (10m): re-evaluate KPI tally; if stable, resume 25% step-ups every 30m; if unstable, revert to previous stable step and open incident
5) Postmortem: 48h mini-ptp, list RCA and immediate mitigations

Contingency knobs (what we can flip fast):
- Traffic routing: cohort percentage adjustments via feature-gate (<1 min)
- Model variant swap: revert to smaller, older model variant (cold rollback ~5–15m if warm caches available)
- Quantization fallback: reduce sequence length or use lower-precision variant to regain throughput
- Cache warming: force KV warm reads for top 100 prefixes during low traffic window

Open questions / notes to self (short bullets):
- Do we surface cost burn to CS/Finance automatically at the warning threshold? (ask finance partner)
- Should we lock Step 3 for 6h before any Step 4 increases? Provisional: yes for first 2 launches.
- Need a short runbook for partner-communication template (support + CSM) — draft in Confluence link above.

Quick comms checklist (pre-launch 24h):
- Publish short-runbook to #prod-ops and create a pinned message
- Confirm oncall schedule + backups for 72h
- Verify traffic-gate feature flag id and rollback button works end-to-end
- Share KPI tally sheet link with launch stakeholders and set hourly snapshot cadence

References & artifacts:
- Confluence design + diagram (see linked artifact)
- JIRA epic ENG-3421 (throttles + feature-gates)
- PR for feature-gate operator: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284

Appendix: Minimal hourly snapshot template to paste into incident channel:
- <HH:MM UTC> | Step=<n> | CohortAlloc=A/B/C/D | P95=<ms> | 5xx=<%> | model-regress=<%> | $/1k=<USD> | tickets=<n> | action=<none|throttle|rollback|model-swap>

End notes (tone):
- This sheet is intentionally terse: the goal is rapid decisioning, not a novel. Keep edits small during launch window; major structural proposals belong in a follow-up doc.
